claims.text: Scientists coordinated worldwide observations of Earth, its atmosphere and solar interactions during the eighteen-month International Geophysical Year.
NASA gives 1 July 1957–31 December 1958; NOAA independently describes the same July-to-December program interval.
The program brought together researchers across national boundaries. World Data Centers helped make the large body of resulting observations accessible.

review.corroboration: NASA’s historical account and NOAA’s observatory history agree on the interval and international coordination. Day-level boundaries come from NASA.
